transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in today because I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Stuff I used to really enjoy, like dance class, hiking, trying out new recipes... even game night. Now they all just sit there like chores I keep putting off. I just don't have the interest I used to, and I wanted to talk to someone about it.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did you first notice you were losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
It's been going on for a while now. I guess... well, it really started after the robbery at that festival job I had. That was about two years and three months ago, so it's been ever since then.

Since it started after the robbery, has this low interest and mood been present pretty much every day without a break, or have there been stretches of weeks or months where you felt back to your normal self in between?
It's been pretty much every day, yeah. I haven't really had any stretches where I felt back to normal. It's just kind of stayed this way without a break since it all happened.

Since the robbery, have you experienced things like unwanted memories or flashbacks of the event, nightmares about it, or found yourself avoiding places, people, or situations that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I do have that happen. Sometimes just a specific sound, like a cash box snapping shut, or if somebody comes up behind me in a kitchen... it brings the robbery back so fast. It's like I can hear the voices again, and my stomach just drops. It feels exactly like it's happening right then.
Besides the loss of interest, have you noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy level, or ability to concentrate since this all began?

Yeah, my concentration has definitely gotten worse. When I try to work on catering forms or, like, a Chamber application, I just can't focus. I'll read the same line over and over again, and nothing sinks in. And then I get stuck on really small choices... like, I can't even figure out what price to put down or which email I should answer first. It's just really hard to think straight.
Since the robbery, have you noticed feeling unusually on edge, easily startled, or overly watchful of your surroundings, even in situations that aren't obviously dangerous?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially in parking lots or, you know, when I'm doing pickups. I'm just always checking who is near me. I make sure I know exactly where my car is and... and I figure out how fast I could leave if I had to. Even if everyone else around me seems totally relaxed, I'm just constantly watching my surroundings.
Since the robbery, have you also been feeling persistently sad, empty, or down most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty like that. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I don't feel down all day every day. It's more just the being on edge and the memories that bother me.

The temporal link to a life-threatening trauma, presence of intrusion, hyperarousal, and numbing/avoidance-type symptoms (loss of interest), combined with explicit denial of persistent depressed mood/emptiness, supports PTSD rather than a primary depressive or adjustment disorder. Duration exceeds 1 month, ruling out Acute Stress Disorder, and symptom severity/chronicity exceeds what would be expected for an adjustment disorder.
